key_terms.meaning: Maps three-address code to target instructions while managing registers and descriptors.
Records which values currently live in each target register.
Records where the current value of a variable can be found.
Maximal straight-line sequence of three-address statements with one entry and one exit.
First statement of a basic block; targets and first statements after jumps are leaders.
Directed graph whose nodes are basic blocks and whose edges are possible control transfers.
Directed acyclic graph for a basic block that shares repeated subexpressions.
Replaces repeated evaluation of an expression by reuse of its earlier computed value.
Evaluates constant expressions at compile time.
Replaces uses of a variable by a known constant value.
Replaces uses of a copied variable by the original variable when safe.
Removes computations whose results are never used.
Replaces an expensive operation by a cheaper equivalent, often multiplication by addition.
Moves an invariant computation out of a loop when it does not change results.
Rewrites code while preserving the function computed for every input.
Applies safe transformations to loop code where repeated execution makes savings large.
Optimization restricted to one basic block or a straight-line region.
Optimization that uses facts about the whole flow graph, not just one block.
Gives the data-flow fact at a block exit from the fact at its entry.
Computes facts at block boundaries by iterating transfer functions over the flow graph.

takeaways: A code generator must map three-address code to target instructions and keep register and address descriptors accurate.
Basic blocks are maximal straight-line runs; leaders start blocks.
The flow graph edges show possible control transfer between basic blocks.
A DAG shares repeated subexpressions within one basic block and exposes copies and dead assignments.
Most optimizations come from removing repeated, useless, constant, copied, or costly work.
Function-preserving transformations keep program results unchanged while improving code.
Loop optimization pays because loop bodies run repeatedly.
Global data-flow analysis iterates transfer functions over the flow graph to a fixed point.
bank_note: Long answers usually stress classification of optimizations, drawing flow graphs and DAGs, and running a data-flow analysis step by step.

glossary.def: Intermediate code with at most one operator per instruction and explicit temporaries.
A machine instruction of the chosen target architecture.
Choosing which variables and temporaries should reside in registers.
Choosing the exact register for each allocated value.
A compiler table entry used by a simple code generator to track register contents or variable locations.
A maximal straight-line sequence of statements with one entry and one exit.
The first statement of a basic block.
A directed graph with basic blocks as nodes and control-transfer edges.
A block with an edge into the given block.
A block with an edge from the given block.
A directed acyclic graph used for a basic block; nodes are values or operations and edges show operand use.
An expression already computed whose operands have not changed.
A computation whose result is never used on any possible execution path.
A variable is live at a point if some path from that point uses its current value before redefining it.
Computing constant expressions during compilation instead of at run time.
Replacing a variable use by a constant known to reach that use.
Replacing a use of a copied variable by the original variable.
Replacing a costly operation by a cheaper equivalent operation.
Moving an expression to a place where it is executed less often.
A local rewrite of a small instruction window into a cheaper equivalent sequence.
An expression inside a loop whose value does not change across loop iterations.
A function that maps data-flow facts at block entry to facts at block exit.
A stable data-flow solution reached when another iteration changes no block fact.
A program rewrite that keeps the same input-output behavior for all inputs.
